Your popularity in high school does not matter. Learning to navigate popularity does, but how popular you actually are will have little to no effect on the rest of your life except for how you let it shape your mind.

In 5-10 years you will likely know almost nobody from high school. The friendships that do last will probably not be the ones you expect to. Friendships formed from sports, popularity, proximity, convenience, fun... those fade quickly. It's only the ones that are formed on what I would call an intellectual level that have a chance of surviving, and that is rare too. People change; if the two of you change too much, even that intellectual connection breaks. Again, the experience of making and having friends is hugely important, but the friendships themselves are far from permanent.

Because of this, cultivate your friendships. Know which ones to let fade or just take a back burner and focus on the ones with a deeper connection. Meet as many people as you can. Get to know as many people as you can. Be open (within reason) to new experiences but be wary of anything addictive. Your life is teeming with potential right now; take advantage of it. In ten years when you look back, you will not regret the things you've done, but the things you didn't do.
